power.claim: Broker reports 3.5 MW in use and electrical/cooling equipment sized for 7 MW. This is infrastructure sizing, not 7 MW vacant transferable IT load or a utility commitment.

advertisedFacts: Current primary listing identifies 12.07 acres, 267,177 SF and $28 million asking price; older press figures differ slightly.
Broker names five telecom carriers and dark fiber routes to 1500 Champa.
Existing office/data-center mix has income; tenant encumbrances and actual vacant white space remain to be reviewed.

buyerMatches.why: Specific platform extension hypothesis: the offered building advertises dark fiber to RadiusDC’s own 1500 Champa hub. RadiusDC’s current Denver page says that hub is fully leased and the company is actively evaluating Denver expansion. A linked Thornton satellite with existing DC infrastructure answers an identified metro-capacity gap more directly than generic rural land.
remainingConditions: Secure transferable fiber rights, physical route diversity and measured RTT to 1500 Champa.
Confirm that a 3.5–7 MW utility-sized building fits the buyer’s next deployment and that vacant/convertible areas support enough critical IT load.
Inspect leases, structural limits, risers, cooling and the economics of a mixed office/DC conversion.
Thornton jurisdiction and permitted use must be verified separately; Denver city rules cannot simply be applied to this parcel.

capitalFit: Institutional $28 million acquisition; propose a sourced acquisition/retrofit to RadiusDC, not a cheap-land assignment.
nextAction: Request rent roll, actual DC/vacant area schedule, utility service documents, fiber IRUs, building plans and current transaction status; ask RadiusDC whether a Champa-connected satellite meets its active expansion requirement.

Model probability of data-center construction separately from probability of an ancillary land purchase.

capitalFit: Potential strategic adjacency or option transaction only if Tract identifies a specific need. Do not spend diligence capital based on neighbor identity alone.
nextAction: Obtain APNs and concept plan; overlay Tract boundary and proposed infrastructure; test whether the offered corner fills an identifiable campus gap.

remainingConditions: Commission actual carrier path/RTT feasibility to the hub CleanArc specifies; fiber count and geographic proximity do not prove latency.

Scope enough first-phase IT power, affordable waterless/liquid-cooling design and utility ramp.

power.claim: Broker says 34.5 kV dual-feed, 11 substations, 10 MW former peak usage and potential 50 MW in approximately 24 months. None establishes current transferable capacity.

advertisedFacts: Former automotive manufacturing plant; broker lists edge data centers as one possible use.

buyerMatches.why: Asset-type fit, not simply an Indiana match: this is a dormant automotive plant with prior high-voltage infrastructure and substantial existing yard/shell. Giga explicitly originates dormant industrial/commercial assets and builds modular facilities on either its own or customer-owned land. A segregated first-phase modular deployment could test whether reusing service infrastructure saves schedule and cost.
remainingConditions: Compare reusable electrical infrastructure and pad areas with Giga pod design; a large obsolete factory may add demolition cost rather than value.
Confirm utility service rights, staged energization, flexible-load terms and customer SLA compatibility.
Establish Giga’s current Midwest/customer mandate; no expressed buyer interest is known.
Verify industrial contamination, cooling, fiber diversity and the value of remaining building improvements.

capitalFit: Too large to assume a founder-funded acquisition. Explore buyer-funded diligence or a seller-backed assignable right only after actual buyer interest.
nextAction: Merge Giga pairing into existing em-amgeneral-mishawaka record, do not add a duplicate site. Request a phased conversion concept and service documents before presenting to Giga.
